trials.name: Footprint-pooled placement head
trials.hypothesis: Keep the starting body. For each brick type, take the max, min and mean of the learned features over its footprint, add the anchor cell's own features, and pass the result through a learned 1x1 layer to get that type's logit. Landing height is a maximum over the footprint and correctness is an all-cells condition, so lining features up with the footprint should make good placements easy to read and help escape the 0.068 level. Refuted if the 2-seed mean is at or below about 0.12.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [(int(f[0]), int(f[1])) for f in spec.footprints]
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(4 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = torch.cat([f, mx, mn, av], dim=1)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[t](h))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 64


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.n_types, self.Y, self.X = spec.n_types, spec.Y, spec.X
        self.n_place = spec.n_place
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels + spec.n_types, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.ctx = nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, WIDTH, 3, padding=1)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B = obs.shape[0]
        m = mask[:, :self.n_place].reshape(B, self.n_types, self.Y, self.X).to(obs.dtype)
        x = torch.cat([obs, m], dim=1)
        f = F.relu(self.conv1(x))
        c = self.ctx(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        f = f + c[:, :, None, None]
        f = F.relu(self.conv2(f))
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 32
BLOCKS = 2


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, w):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(w, w, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(w, w, 3, padding=1)

        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)

            av = F.avg_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = torch.cat([f, mx, mn, av], dim=1)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[t](h))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))

For each brick type, the per-layer features are pooled over the footprint (max and min). The body's footprint features then produce a softmax over layers that selects which layer's features to use. import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 32
BLOCKS = 2
LW = 16


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, w):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(w, w, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(w, w, 3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return F.relu(x + self.c2(F.relu(self.c1(x))))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.footprints = [(int(f[0]), int(f[1])) for f in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*[Block(WIDTH) for _ in range(BLOCKS)])
        self.layer_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(7, LW, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(LW, LW, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.sel_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(4 * WIDTH, spec.Z, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(4 * WIDTH + 2 * LW, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        f = self.blocks(self.stem(obs))
        b = obs[:, 0:Z]
        t_ = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        m = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        e = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        bb = F.pad(b, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :Z]
        tb = F.pad(t_, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :Z]
        zpos = (torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype) / Z).view(1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        per = torch.stack([b, t_, m, e, bb, tb, zpos], dim=2).reshape(B * Z, 7, Y, X)
        L = self.layer_conv(per)
        outs = []
        for k, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = torch.cat([f, mx, mn, av], dim=1)
            lp = F.pad(L, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            lmx = F.max_pool2d(lp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            lmn = -F.max_pool2d(-lp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            lf = torch.cat([lmx, lmn], dim=1).reshape(B, Z, 2 * LW, Y, X)
            q = torch.softmax(self.sel_heads[k](h), dim=1)
            sel = (q.unsqueeze(2) * lf).sum(1)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[k](torch.cat([h, sel], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 32
BLOCKS = 2
HEADS = 4


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, w):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(w, w, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(w, w, 3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return F.relu(x + self.c2(F.relu(self.c1(x))))


class CellAttn(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, w, heads):
        super().__init__()
        self.h = heads
        self.d = w // heads
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(w)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(w, 3 * w)
        self.out = nn.Linear(w, w)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(w)
        self.ff1 = nn.Linear(w, 2 * w)
        self.ff2 = nn.Linear(2 * w, w)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.out.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.out.bias)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.ff2.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.ff2.bias)

    def forward(self, f):
        B, C, Y, X = f.shape
        N = Y * X
        x = f.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)
        q, k, v = self.qkv(self.norm1(x)).chunk(3, dim=-1)
        q = q.reshape(B, N, self.h, self.d).transpose(1, 2)
        k = k.reshape(B, N, self.h, self.d).transpose(1, 2)
        v = v.reshape(B, N, self.h, self.d).transpose(1, 2)
        a = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-1, -2)) / math.sqrt(self.d), dim=-1)
        o = torch.matmul(a, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, N, C)
        x = x + self.out(o)
        x = x + self.ff2(F.relu(self.ff1(self.norm2(x))))
        return x.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, C, Y, X)


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [(int(f[0]), int(f[1])) for f in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*[Block(WIDTH) for _ in range(BLOCKS)])
        self.attn = CellAttn(WIDTH, HEADS)
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(4 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.attn(self.blocks(self.stem(obs)))
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = torch.cat([f, mx, mn, av], dim=1)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[t](h))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            rp = F.pad(f, (1, dx, 1, dy))
            rmx = F.max_pool2d(rp, (dy + 2, dx + 2), stride=1)
            rav = F.avg_pool2d(rp, (dy + 2, dx + 2), stride=1)
            h = torch.cat([f, mx, mn, av, rmx, rav], dim=1)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[t](h))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 32
BLOCKS = 2
LW = 8


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, w):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(w, w, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(w, w, 3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return F.relu(x + self.c2(F.relu(self.c1(x))))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.footprints = [(int(f[0]), int(f[1])) for f in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*[Block(WIDTH) for _ in range(BLOCKS)])
        self.layer_conv = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(7, LW, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(LW, LW, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.sel_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(4 * WIDTH, spec.Z, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(4 * WIDTH + 2 * LW, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, C, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        f = self.blocks(self.stem(obs))
        b = obs[:, 0:Z]
        t_ = obs[:, Z:2 * Z]
        m = obs[:, 2 * Z:3 * Z]
        e = obs[:, 3 * Z:4 * Z]
        bb = F.pad(b, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :Z]
        tb = F.pad(t_, (0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :Z]
        zpos = (torch.arange(Z, device=obs.device, dtype=obs.dtype) / Z).view(1, Z, 1, 1).expand(B, Z, Y, X)
        per = torch.stack([b, t_, m, e, bb, tb, zpos], dim=2).reshape(B * Z, 7, Y, X)
        L = self.layer_conv(per)
        outs = []
        for k, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = torch.cat([f, mx, mn, av], dim=1)
            lp = F.pad(L, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            lmx = F.max_pool2d(lp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            lmn = -F.max_pool2d(-lp, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            lf = torch.cat([lmx, lmn], dim=1).reshape(B, Z, 2 * LW, Y, X)
            q = torch.softmax(self.sel_heads[k](h), dim=1)
            sel = (q.unsqueeze(2) * lf).sum(1)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[k](torch.cat([h, sel], dim=1)))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.hypothesis: r2c1, but the pooled board summary scales the footprint features (h times 1 + gamma(g)) before each type's logit. The gamma layer starts at zero, so the network begins exactly as r2c1. The rest of the board decides which local cues matter, for example finishing lower layers first or stopping late in the episode. import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

WIDTH = 32
BLOCKS = 2


class Block(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, w):
        super().__init__()
        self.c1 = nn.Conv2d(w, w, 3, padding=1)
        self.c2 = nn.Conv2d(w, w, 3, padding=1)

    def forward(self, x):
        return F.relu(x + self.c2(F.relu(self.c1(x))))


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.footprints = [(int(f[0]), int(f[1])) for f in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.blocks = nn.Sequential(*[Block(WIDTH) for _ in range(BLOCKS)])
        self.type_heads = nn.ModuleList([nn.Conv2d(4 * WIDTH, 1, 1) for _ in self.footprints])
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.film = nn.Linear(64, 4 * WIDTH)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.film.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.film.bias)
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.blocks(self.stem(obs))
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        gamma = self.film(g)[:, :, None, None]
        outs = []
        for t, (dy, dx) in enumerate(self.footprints):
            p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            av = F.avg_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            h = torch.cat([f, mx, mn, av], dim=1)
            h = h * (1.0 + gamma)
            outs.append(self.type_heads[t](h))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1).flatten(1)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The starting network's four seeds scored 0.068 three times and 0.258 once. That means 35/512 three times: training seems to get stuck at the same easy level, and only some seeds move past it. Each trial gets about 32 updates of 4,096 steps. A network smaller than the start costs nothing extra in steps, but a larger one cuts steps in proportion. So I'm looking for changes that make good placements easier to learn without adding compute. To score a placement, the agent must work out how high a brick lands, which is the highest column under its whole footprint. It must then check that this layer's target cells match and are still missing. The starting head reads only the anchor cell's features and has a 5x5 view. Ideas for this round: (A) pool features over each brick's footprint, (B) a deeper residual body that sees the whole grid at the same compute, (C) give the network the legal-move mask and whole-board context.
analyses.2: Two different changes both beat the starting architecture's 4-seed mean of 0.116. The footprint-pooled placement head (r1c1) scored 0.31 with seeds 0.39 and 0.24. The deep, narrow residual body (r1c2) scored 0.28 with seeds 0.34 and 0.23. All four of these seeds cleared the 0.068 failure level, so both changes probably help, but the gap between them is within noise. r1c3 (mask input plus global broadcast) stayed at 0.068 on both seeds, matching the stuck outcome seen in 3 of the 4 starting seeds. That trial changed two things at once, so it doesn't show which part hurt. The next steps are to combine the two winners, test whether the footprint head needs more capacity, and try a head built around the drop physics: the brick lands at a layer set by the footprint's maximum height, so the head should check the target at that layer. All three candidates stay near 1x compute to keep most of the step budget.
analyses.3: Footprint pooling in the placement head is the clearest gain: the starting body went from 0.068 to 0.31 with it. A deeper residual body also helped (0.28). Together in r2c1 they reached 0.495, and both seeds agreed (0.496 and 0.494), so the run seems to escape the stuck 0.068 level reliably. The landing-layer attention head (r2c3, 0.45) did no better than r2c1 and took twice as long. Making the placement head nonlinear (r2c2, 0.10) did badly, though it also ran 25% fewer steps on the weaker body. Mask input with a plain global broadcast (r1c3) stayed at the stuck level. Depth and receptive field look like the levers that work. My next tests: a larger view at the same compute (dilation), one more residual block, and global mixing through self-attention, which is a different mechanism from r1c3's broadcast. Each test is one change on top of r2c1.
analyses.4: The footprint-aligned placement head is the clearest gain: about 0.07 to 0.31 on the starting body, and 0.28 to 0.50 on the residual body. r2c1 (residual width 32, footprint max/min/mean head) is best at 0.495, and its two seeds agree. Every trial whose compute went above about 1.2x the starting network collapsed to about 0.10 (r2c2, r3c2), so lost steps cost a lot here. A network cheaper than the starting one gets no extra steps, so there is about 10% compute slack to use. The per-layer landing head (r2c3) scored 0.45, within noise of r2c1 (one seed reached 0.51), but it cost 8% of the steps. Dilation (0.39) and cell attention (0.31, noisy) did not help. For the last round I keep r2c1's body and compute at or below 1.0x, and try cheap additions to the placement head.
